<td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">3.11</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Provisions</div> </div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank recognizes a provision if and only if the following circumstances are met: (a)&#160;the Bank has a present obligation as a result of a past event; (b)&#160;it is probable (i.e. it is more likely than not) that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits will be required to settle the obligation; and (c)&#160;a reliable estimate can be made of the amount of the obligation. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In order to determine the amount of provisions, the risks and uncertainties were considered taking into account the opinion of independent and internal legal advisors of the Bank. Where the effect of the time value of money is material, the provisions shall be discounted using a pre-tax rate that reflects, if applicable, current risks specific to the liability. When the discount is recognized, the effect of the provision derived from the lapse of time is accounted for as &#8220;Interest expense&#8221; in the statement of income. Based on the analysis carried out, the Bank recognized as provision the amount of the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the end of each fiscal year. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The provisions accounted for by the Bank are reviewed at the end of each reporting period or fiscal year, as applicable, and adjusted to reflect the current best available estimate. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, provisions are recognized with specific allocation to be used only for the expenditures for which they were originally recognized. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the event: a) the obligation is possible; or b) it is not probable that an outflow of resources will be required for the Bank to settle the obligation; or c) the amount of the obligation cannot be estimated reliably, the contingent liability shall not be recognized and shall be disclosed in notes. Nevertheless, when the possibility of an outflow of resources is remote, no disclosures shall be made. </div> </ix:nonNumeric> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForFeeAndCommissionIncomeAndExpenseExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_112971818" id="ixv-51284">

The majority of Bank&#8217;s income and expenses are related to financial instruments, in general recorded using the effective interest method. <td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Deferred income tax: it is assessed based on the separate Financial Statements of the Bank and of each of its subsidiaries and reflects the effects of temporary differences between the carrying amount of an asset or liability in the statement of financial position and its tax base. The measurement of deferred tax liabilities and deferred tax assets reflects the tax consequences that will follow from the manner in which the Bank and its subsidiaries expect, at the end of the reporting period, to recover or settle the carrying amount of their assets and liabilities. <td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Fiduciary activities and investment management</div> </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The Bank renders custody, administration, investment management and advisory services to third parties that originate the holding or placement of assets in the name of such third parties. These assets and income on them are not included in these consolidated Financial Statements, since they are not owned by the Bank. The commissions derived from these activities are accounted for as &#8220;Commissions income&#8221; in the consolidated statement of income. See also Notes 45, 46 and 49. </div></div></div> </ix:nonNumeric> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Accounting judgments, estimates and assumptions</div></div></div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The preparation of these consolidated Financial Statements requires the Bank&#8217;s Management to consider significant accounting judgments, estimates and assumptions that impact on the reported assets and liabilities, income, revenues and expenses, as well as the assessment and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities, as of the end of the fiscal year. The Bank&#8217;s reported amounts are based on the best estimate regarding the probability of occurrence of different future events and, therefore, the uncertainties associated with the estimates and assumptions made by the Bank&#8217;s Management may drive in the future to final amounts that may differ from those estimates and may require material adjustments to the reported amounts of the affected assets and liabilities. </div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">In certain cases, the Financial Statements prepared in accordance with the IFRS, require that the assets and liabilities to be recognized and/or presented at their fair value. The fair value is the amount at which an asset can be exchanged, or at which a liability can be settled, in mutual independent terms and conditions between participants of the principal market (or most advantageous market) duly informed and willing to transact in an orderly and current transaction. When prices in active markets are available, the Bank has used them as basis for valuation. When prices in active markets are not available, the Bank estimates those values as values based on the best available information, including the use of models and other assessment techniques (for additional information regarding fair value estimates see Note 13). This kind of estimates also applies to the measurement of acquired identifiable assets and liabilities assumed as a consequence of business combinations (see Note 14). </div></div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In estimating accrued taxes, the Bank assesses the relative risks of the appropriate tax treatment considering judicial and regulatory guidance in the context of the tax position. Because of the complexity of tax laws and regulations, interpretation can be difficult and subject to legal judgment. It is possible that others, given the same information, may reach different reasonable conclusions regarding the estimated amounts of accrued taxes (for additional information regarding income tax see Note 29). </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the normal course of business, the Bank is a party to lawsuits of various types. In Note 50, contingent liabilities are disclosed with respect to existing or potential claims, lawsuits and other legal proceedings, and is booked an accrual for litigation when it is probable that future costs will be incurred and these costs can be reasonably estimated. </div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The measurement of impairment losses under IFRS 9 across all categories of financial instruments requires judgment, in particular, the estimation of the amount and timing of future cash flows and collateral values when determining impairment losses and the assessment of a significant increase in credit risk. These estimates are driven by a number of factors, changes that can result in different levels of allowances (for additional information regarding impairment losses under IFRS 9, see Notes 3.2.4 and 52.1.1). </div></div></div> <ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForNewStandardsAdoptedInTheFiscalYearExplanatoryPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_112969250" id="ixv-51469"> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">New standards adopted in the fiscal year</div></div></div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the fiscal year beginning on January&#160;1, 2023, the following amendments to IFRS are effective: </div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;"><ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude></div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center"><ix:exclude>3<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">4</div></ix:exclude></div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation> </div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_112969250" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112969250_1"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112972202_79" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112972202_80"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112972202_80" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112972202_81"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112972202_81" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112972202_82"><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation> </ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112972202_82"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112969250_1"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><ix:exclude>BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 1 &#8220;Presentation of Financial Statements&#8221; and IFRS Practice Statement 2 &#8211; Disclosures to accounting policies</div>: </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The amendments require that an entity discloses its material accounting policies, instead of its significant accounting policies. They also explain how an entity can identify material accounting policy information and give examples of when accounting policy information is likely to be material. Therefore, a guidance with explanations and examples denominated &#8220;four-step materiality process&#8221; was as described in the Practice Statement 2. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This amendment did not have a material impact on the disclosures of these consolidated Financial Statements or the annual consolidated Financial Statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 8 &#8220;Accounting policies, changes in accounting estimates and Errors&#8221; &#8211; Definition of Accounting Estimates</div>: </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The amendments clarify the distinction between changes in accounting estimates and changes in accounting policies and the correction of errors. Also, they clarify how entities use measurement techniques and inputs to develop accounting estimates. The amended standard clarifies that the effects on an accounting estimate of a change in an input or a change in a measurement technique are changes in accounting estimates if they do not result from the correction of prior period errors. The previous definition of a change in accounting estimate specified that changes in accounting estimates may result from new information or new developments. Therefore, such changes are not corrections of errors. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This amendment would be applicable if the Bank performs a change in an accounting estimate, but it is not expected to have a material impact on the Financial Statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 12 &#8220;Income Tax&#8221; &#8211; Deferred Tax related to Assets and Liabilities arising from a Single Transaction</div>: </div><div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The IASB issued amendments to IAS 12, which narrow the scope of the initial recognition exception under IAS 12, so that it no longer applies to transactions that give rise to equal taxable and deductible temporary differences. The amendments clarify that where payments that settle a liability are deductible for tax purposes, it is a matter of professional judgment (having considered the applicable tax law) whether such deductions are attributable for tax purposes to the liability recognized in the Financial Statements (and interest expense) or to the related asset component (and interest expense). Professional judgment is important in determining whether any temporary differences exist on initial recognition of the asset and liability. </div></div></div><div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">This amendment did not have a material impact on the Financial Statements. </div></div></div><div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 12 &#8220;Income Tax&#8221; &#8211; International Tax Reform-Pillar Two Model Rules: </div></div></div><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"></div></div><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The IASB issued International Tax Reform - Pillar Two Model Rules in May 2023. This amendment introduces a temporary exception to the accounting for deferred tax assets and liabilities related to Pillar Two income taxes. The amendment also adds targeted disclosure requirements for affected entities, including information about an entity&#8217;s exposure to Pillar Two income taxes (before Pillar Two legislation is effective) and current tax expense related to Pillar Two income taxes (when Pillar Two legislation is effective). </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">At the day of these consolidated Financial Statements, the aforementioned Tax Reform has not been enacted in Argentina. Therefore, this amendment did not have impact on the disclosures of these consolidated Financial Statements. </div></div></div> <div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"> </div></div></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForNewAccountingPronouncementsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-51528"> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">New pronouncements</div></div></div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The new and amended standards and interpretations that are issued, but not yet effective, up to the date of issuance of these consolidated Financial Statements are disclosed below. The Bank intends to adopt these standards, if applicable, when they become effective. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:7%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">a)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Amendments to IFRS 16 &#8220;Leases&#8221; &#8211; Sale and Leaseback: the amendment to IFRS 16 specifies the requirements that a seller-lessee uses in measuring the lease liability arising in a sale and leaseback transaction, to ensure the seller-lessee does not recognize any amount of the gain or loss that relates to the right of use it retains. The amendment does not prescribe specific measurement requirements for lease liabilities arising from a leaseback. The initial measurement of the lease liability arising from a leaseback may result in a seller-lessee determining &#8216;lease payments&#8217; that are different from the general definition of lease payments. The seller lessee will need to develop and apply an accounting policy that results in information that is relevant and reliable in accordance with IAS 8. This amendment is applicable as of January&#160;1, 2024. The Bank does not expect this standard to have a material impact on the Financial Statements. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

This amendment is applicable as of January&#160;1, 2024. The Bank does not expect this standard to have a material impact on the Financial Statements. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Amendments to IAS 21 &#8220;Lack of Exchangeability&#8221;: the amendments to this standard will allow an entity to evaluate whether a currency is exchangeable and how to determine a spot exchange rate when exchangeability is lacking. This amendment is applicable as of January&#160;1, 2025. The Bank is evaluating the effects that this amendment would cause in these consolidated Financial Statements. </div></td></tr></table> </ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">3<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">5</div></div> </div></div> <div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div> <hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> </div></div> <div> <div> <div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"> <div style="text-align:center"> <div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES </div></div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfOtherProvisionsContingentLiabilitiesAndContingentAssetsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-51570">

margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;text-indent: 0px;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center;text-indent: 0px;">3<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">7</div></div> </div> </div> </div> <div></div> </div> <div> <div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"> <div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div> <hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> </div> </div> </div> <div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES </div></div><div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfDerivativeFinancialInstrumentsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-52787">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td id="fin89987_12" style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">6.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">DERIVATIVE FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank performs derivative transactions for trading purposes through Futures and Forwards. These are contractual agreements to buy or sell a specific financial instrument at a given price and a fixed date in the future. Future contracts, in turn, correspond to transactions for standardized amounts, executed in a regulated market and subject to daily cash margin requirements. Forward contracts are customized contracts traded on an over-the-counter market. The main differences in risks associated with these types of contracts are the credit risk and the liquidity risk. In forward contracts there is counterparty risk since the Bank has credit exposure to counterparties of the agreements. The credit risk related to futures contracts is deemed very low because daily cash margin requirements help guarantee these contracts are always fulfilled. In addition, forward contracts are generally settled in gross terms and, therefore, they are deemed to have a higher settlement risk than future contracts that, unless they are chosen to be performed by delivery, are settled on a net basis. Both types of contracts expose the Bank to market risk. See in addition Notes 5 and 10. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At the beginning, derivatives often imply only a mutual exchange of promises with little or no investment. Nevertheless, these instruments frequently imply high levels of leverage and are quite volatile. A relatively small movement in the value of the unde<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">rlyi</div>ng asset could have a significant impact in profit or loss. Furthermore, over-the-counter derivatives may expose the Bank to risks related to the absence of an exchange market in which to close an open position. The Bank&#8217;s exposure for derivative contracts is monitored on a regular basis as part of its general risk management framework. Information on the Bank&#8217;s credit risk management objectives and policies is included in Note 52. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Notional values indicate the amount of the underlying pending transactions at year end and are not indicative of either the market risk or the credit risk. The fair value of the derivative financial instruments recognized as assets or liabilities in the consolidated statement of financial position is presented as follows. Changes in fair values were accounted for in profit or loss, the breakdown of which is disclosed in Note 34. </div><div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DisclosureOfNotionalAndFairValueAmountsOfDerivativeFinancialInstrumentsTableTextBlock" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-52801">

<td>&#160;</td></tr></table></ix:nonNumeric> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Derivatives held for trading are generally related to products offered by the Bank to its customers. The Bank shall also take positions expecting to benefit from favorable changes in prices, rates or indexes, i.e. take advantage of the high level of leverage of these contracts to obtain yields, assuming at the same time high market risk. Additionally, they may be held for arbitrage, i.e. to obtain a benefit free of risk for the combination of a derivative product and a portfolio of financial assets, trying to benefit from anomalous situations in the prices of assets in the markets. </div><div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div></ix:nonNumeric> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">3<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">8</div></div></div></div><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><div style="text-align: center; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES </div></div></div></div><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfRepurchaseAndReverseRepurchaseAgreementsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_112968846" id="ixv-53218"><div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div></div>

<td style="width: 7%; vertical-align: top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">7.</div></div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align: top;text-align:left;"><div style="text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">REPURCHASE AGREEMENTS </div></div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="clear:both;max-height:0pt;text-indent: 0px;"></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent: 0px;">Securities sold under agreements to repurchase at a specified future date are not derecognized from the statement of financial position as the Bank retains substantially all of the risks and rewards of ownership. The corresponding cash received is recognized in the consolidated statement of financial position as an asset with a corresponding obligation to return it, including accrued interest as a liability within cash collateral on securities lent and repurchase agreements, reflecting the transaction&#8217;s economic substance as a loan to the Bank. The difference between the sale and repurchase prices is treated as interest expense and is accrued over the life of agreement using the effective interest method. When the counterparty has the right to sell or re-pledge the securities, the Bank reclassifies those securities in its statement of financial position to &#8220;Financial Assets delivered as guarantee&#8221;. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent: 0px;">Conversely, securities purchased under agreements to resell at a specified future date are not recognized in the statement of financial position. The consideration paid, including accrued interest, is recorded in the statement of financial position, within cash collateral on securities borrowed and reverse repurchase agreements, reflecting the transaction&#8217;s economic substance as a loan by the Bank. The difference between the purchase and resale prices is recorded in net interest income and is accrued over the life of the agreement using the effective interest method. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-indent: 0px;">If securities purchased under an agreement to resell are subsequently sold to third parties, the obligation to return the securities is recorded in &#8220;Liabilities at fair value through profit or loss&#8221;.<br/></div></ix:nonNumeric><div style="margin: 6pt 2% 0pt 7%; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;text-indent: 0px;"><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_112968846" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112968846_1"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">As of December&#160;31, 2023 and 2022, the Bank has repurchase agreements of government and private securities, in absolute value, fo</div></div>r <ix:nonFraction name="bma:TransactionCostForReverseRepurchasesOfSecurities" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_GovernmentSecuritiesMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119273">639,183,710</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:TransactionCostForReverseRepurchasesOfSecurities" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2022_GovernmentSecuritiesMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119274">192,852,624</ix:nonFraction>, <div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">respectively. <td id="fin89987_15" style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">9.</div></div></td>

This classification is made pursuant to the expressed in Note 3 &#8220;Basis for the preparation of these Financial Statements and applicable accounting standards&#8221;. Additionally, Note 13 explains the information related to the valuation process. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Moreover, the Bank applies the impairment requirements for guarantees granted, undrawn commitments of credit cards and checking accounts, letter of credits, which are not recognized in the consolidated statement of financial position. This impairment is disclosed in the consolidated statement of income as &#8220;Other operating expenses&#8221;. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the purpose of assessing the Bank&#8217;s credit risk exposure and identifying material credit risk concentration, disclosures regarding credit risk of financial assets and items not recognized in the statement of financial position are as follows. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfCreditRiskExposureExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-53519">

<td id="fin89987_19" style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">13.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">FAIR VALUE QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES </div></div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The fair value is the amount at which an asset can be exchanged, or at which a liability can be settled, in mutual independent terms and conditions between participants of the principal market (or the most advantageous market) who are duly informed and willing to transact in an orderly and current transaction, at the measurement date under the current market conditions whether the price is directly observable or estimated using a valuation technique under the assumption that the Bank is an ongoing business. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">When a financial instrument is quoted in a liquid and active market, its price in the market in a real transaction provides the most reliable evidence of its fair value. Nevertheless, when there is no quoted price in the market or it cannot be evidence of the fair value of such instrument, in order to determine such fair value, the entities may use the market value of another instrument with similar characteristics, the analysis of discounted cash flows or other applicable techniques, which shall be significantly affected by the assumptions used. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Notwithstanding the above, the Bank&#8217;s Management has used its best judgment to estimate the fair values of its financial instruments; any technique to perform such estimate implies certain inherent fragility level. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Fair value hierarchy</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank uses the following hierarchy to determine and disclose the fair value of financial instruments, according to the valuation technique applied: </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:10%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Level 1: quoted prices (unadjusted) observable in active markets that the Bank accesses to at the measurement day for identical assets or liabilities. The Bank considers markets as active only if there are sufficient trading activities with respect to the volume and liquidity of the identical assets or liabilities and when there are binding and exercisable price quotes available at each reporting period. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:10%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Level 2: Valuation techniques for which the data and variables having a significant impact on the determination of the fair value recognized or disclosed are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. Such inputs include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices for identical instruments in inactive markets and observable inputs other than quoted prices, such as interest rates and yield curves, implied volatilities, and credit spreads. In addition, adjustments to level 2 inputs may be required for the condition or location of the asset or the extent to which it relates to items that are comparable to the valued instrument. However, if such adjustments are based on unobservable inputs that are significant to the entire measurement, the Bank will classify the instruments as Level 3. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><ix:exclude>BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES</ix:exclude> </div></div> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt"><ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude></div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Description of the valuation process</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The fair value of instruments categorized as Level 1 was assessed by using quoted prices effective at the end of each fiscal year in active markets for identical assets or liabilities, if representative. Currently, for most of the government and private securities, there are two principal markets in which the Bank operates: BYMA and MAE. Additionally, in the case of derivatives, both MAE and Mercado a T&#233;rmino de Rosario SA (ROFEX) are deemed active markets. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On the other hand, for certain assets and liabilities that do not have an active market, categorized as Level 2, the Bank used valuation techniques that included the use of market transactions performed under mutual independent terms and conditions, between interested and duly informed parties, provided that they are available as well as references to the current fair value of another instrument being substantially similar, or otherwise the analysis of cash flows discounted at rates built from market information of similar instruments. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, certain assets and liabilities included in this category were valued using price quotes of identical instruments in &#8220;less active markets&#8221;. </div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 7%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Finally, the Bank has categorized as level 3 those assets and liabilities for which there are no identical or similar transactions in the market. To determine the market value of these instruments the Bank used valuation techniques based on own assumptions. For this approach, the Bank mainly used the cash flow discount model. </div></div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of December&#160;31, 2023 and 2022, the Bank has neither changed the techniques nor the assumptions used to estimate the fair value of the financial instruments. </div> <ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DisclosureOfFairValueMeasurementOfFinancialAssetsAndLiabilitiesDisaggregatedByValuationTechniqueExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-68701"> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Below is the reconciliation between the amounts at the beginning and at the end of the fiscal year of the financial assets recognized at fair value categorized as level 3: </div> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td>&#160;</td></tr></table></ix:continuation> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The goodwill generated by the acquisition of <div style="text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Macro Agro</div> SAU amounted to <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:GoodwillRecognisedAsOfAcquisitionDate" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120430">339,958</ix:nonFraction>. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In accordance with the share purchase contract, the transaction price was set at USD <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:AcquisitiondateFairValueOfTotalConsiderationTransferred" contextRef="PAsOn05_18_2023_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120431">5,218,800</ix:nonFraction>, which will be paid in variable annual installments using the proceeds from the dividends of <div style="text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Macro Agro</div> SAU. Thus, the Bank assigns <ix:nonFraction name="bma:PercentageOfDividendRightsAssignableOrAssigned" contextRef="PAsOn05_18_2023_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120432">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the rights over the dividends in favor of the seller, up to the full payment of the purchase price. Each installment will become due within <ix:nonNumeric name="bma:InstalmentAmountTermWithinWhichTheSameShallBeSettled" contextRef="P05_18_2023To05_18_2023_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" id="ixv-120433">fifteen days</ix:nonNumeric> as from the Shareholders&#8217; Meeting approval of <div style="text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Macro Agro</div> SAU Financial Statements. The first installment will become due in 2024. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To measure the liabilities arising from this transaction the Bank estimated the Company&#8217;s future income, discounting them at its own business rate. As a consequence, at the acquisition date, the liability amounted to USD <ix:nonFraction name="bma:LiabilitiesDiscountedToPresentValue" contextRef="PAsOn05_18_2023_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120434">2,973,375</ix:nonFraction>. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On September&#160;29, 2023, <div style="text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Macro Agro</div> SAU distributed cash dividends amounting to <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DividendsReceivedClassifiedAsInvestingActivities" contextRef="P09_29_2023To09_29_2023_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120435">440,000</ix:nonFraction> (not restated). Those dividends were received by Banco Macro SA on October&#160;2, 2023. As it was explained in the previous paragraphs, dividends were used to pay the liability arising from the purchase, which decreased by USD <ix:nonFraction name="bma:DecreaseInConsiderationPayableToAcquiree" contextRef="P09_29_2023To09_29_2023_MacroAgroSAUMemberifrsfullBusinessCombinationsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120436">558,651.70</ix:nonFraction>. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

In this sense, the Bank supervises the operating segment income (loss) for the fiscal year in order to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segment and assess its performance, which is measured on a consistent basis with the profit or loss in the Financial Statements. </div> <div style="font-size: 18pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div> </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfIncomeTaxExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_112972499" id="ixv-85956">

font-size:8pt">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Fiscal years 2019 and 2020</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As decided by the Board of Directors in the meeting held on May&#160;11, 2020, considering certain case law on the matter assessed by its legal counsel and tax advisors, on May&#160;26 of that year, the Bank filed with the Administraci&#243;n Federal de Ingresos P&#250;blicos (AFIP, for its acronym in Spanish) its annual income tax return considering the total effect of the inflation adjustment on income tax (see section a) iv) of this note). As a result, the current income tax determined by Banco Macro SA for fiscal year 2019 amounted to <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:CurrentTaxExpenseIncomeAndAdjustmentsForCurrentTaxOfPriorPeriods" contextRef="P01_01_2019To12_31_2019_BancoMacroSaBizlandSauUnionTransitoriaMemberdeiLegalEntityAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121652">7,002,124</ix:nonFraction> (not restated). The same criterion was applied to determine the annual income tax report for 2020, which generated accrued income tax for Banco Macro SA for such fiscal year that amounted to <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:CurrentTaxExpenseIncomeAndAdjustmentsForCurrentTaxOfPriorPeriods" contextRef="P01_01_2020To12_31_2020_BancoMacroSaBizlandSauUnionTransitoriaMemberdeiLegalEntityAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121653">9,933,210</ix:nonFraction> (not restated). </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, on July&#160;23, 2021, the Bank filed a reimbursement action with the AFIP requesting that <ix:nonFraction name="bma:ReimbursementOfIncomeTaxAmount" contextRef="P07_23_2021To07_23_2021_TaxYearTwoThousandAndTwentyMemberBMATaxPeriodAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121654">254,305</ix:nonFraction> (not restated) paid as income tax for the 2020 tax period be reimbursed. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As to the tax periods mentioned in previous paragraphs, on November&#160;1, 2021, the AFIP notified the beginning of an income tax audit, which is in progress. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Along with the filings mentioned in the first paragraph of this section, on December&#160;28, 2021, the Bank filed petitions for declaratory judgment with the Federal Administrative Contentious Court for the periods under analysis. The file 22274/2021, for the fiscal year 2019, is in process in Court No.&#160;12 and the file 22278/2021, for the fiscal year 2020, is in process in Court No.&#160;1. </div> <div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Fiscal year 2021</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On October&#160;17, 2022, Banco Macro SA filed a reimbursement action with the AFIP requesting that <ix:nonFraction name="bma:ReimbursementOfIncomeTaxAmount" contextRef="P10_17_2022To10_17_2022_TaxYearTwoThousandAndTwentyOneMemberBMATaxPeriodAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121655">382,189</ix:nonFraction> (not restated) paid as income tax for the 2021 tax period be reimbursed. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On January&#160;3, 2023, the AFIP notified the beginning of an income tax audit related to the abovementioned fiscal year, which is in progress. </div> <div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Fiscal year 2022</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On June&#160;30, 2023, Banco Macro SA filed a reimbursement action with the AFIP requesting that 654,673 (not restated) paid as income tax for the 2022 tax period be reimbursed. </div> <div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Reimbursement actions &#8211; Fiscal years 2013 to 2017 and 2018</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On October&#160;24, 2019, Banco Macro SA filed with the AFIP-DGI (Argentine tax authorities) two reimbursement actions under the terms established by the first paragraph of section 81, Law No.&#160;11683 requesting the reimbursement of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:IncomeTaxesPaidRefund" contextRef="P10_24_2019To10_24_2019_BancoMacroSaBizlandSauUnionTransitoriaMemberdeiLegalEntityAxis_FiscalYearTwoThousandThirteenToTwoThousandSeventeenMemberBMATaxPeriodAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121656">4,782,766</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:IncomeTaxesPaidRefund" contextRef="P10_24_2019To10_24_2019_BancoMacroSaBizlandSauUnionTransitoriaMemberdeiLegalEntityAxis_FiscalYearTwoThousandAndEighteenMemberBMATaxPeriodAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121657">5,015,451</ix:nonFraction> (not restated amounts) paid to tax authorities as income tax during tax periods 2013 through 2017 and 2018, respectively, arising from the impossibility to apply the adjustment for inflation and other adjustment mechanisms set forth by income tax Law (prior to the amendments introduced by Laws No.&#160;27430 and 27468 for periods 2013 through 2017, and as revised in 2019 and amended for the 2018 tax period), plus the related compensatory interest (SIGEA [case and file management system] files No.&#160;19144-14224/2019 and 19144-14222/2019). Since tax authorities have not yet issued a resolution with respect to the abovementioned claims, on August&#160;7, 2020, the Bank filed both reimbursement requests under the terms of section 81, Law No.&#160;11683 with the Federal Contentious and Administrative Trial Courts, which are pending in Courts No.&#160;8 and 2 of such jurisdiction, respectively (cases No.&#160;11285/2020 and 11296/2020). Currently, in connection with the file for the fiscal year 2018, the evidence stage is closed and the process for allegation was delivered. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In connection with the tax periods mentioned in the previous paragraph, on December&#160;19, 2019, the AFIP notified the beginning of the income tax audit for the 2018 tax period, and on May&#160;3, 2021, it notified the beginning of the income tax audit for periods 2013 through 2017. On October&#160;4, 2021, the AFIP ended the audit for periods 2013 through 2017 as the Bank had exercised in due time its right to resort to justice, and that the admission of reimbursement is subject to a court decision. </div> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div> </ix:continuation> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">7<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">4</div></div> </div> </div> <div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div> <hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> <div style="text-align:center"> <div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES </div></div> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfInterestIncomeExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-86949">

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Financial trusts for investment purposes </div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Debt securities include mainly prepayments towards the placement price of provisional trust securities of the financial trusts under public and private offerings (Confibono and Secubono). The assets managed for these trusts are mainly related to securitizations of consumer loans. Trust securities are placed once the public offering is authorized by the CNV. Upon expiry of the placement period, once all trust securities have been placed on the market, the Bank recovers the disbursements made, plus an agreed-upon compensation. If after making the best efforts, such trust securities cannot be placed, the Bank will retain the definitive trust securities. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, the Bank&#8217;s portfolio is completed with financial trusts for investment purposes, trust securities of definitive financial trusts in public and private offering (Confibono, Secubono, Supercanal, Payway cobro anticipado, Solidario de Infraestructura Nasa IV, Moni Mobile and Red Surcos) and certificates of participation (Arfintech). </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of December&#160;31, 2023 and 2022, debt securities and certificates of participation in financial trusts for investment, amounted to <ix:nonFraction name="bma:ParticipationCertificatesAndDebtSecuritiesOfFinancialTrustsHeld" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122096">877,222</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:ParticipationCertificatesAndDebtSecuritiesOfFinancialTrustsHeld" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122097">2,961,172</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">According to the latest accounting information available as of the date of issuance of these consolidated Financial Statements, the corpus assets of the trusts exceed the carrying amount in the related proportions. </div> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Trusts created using financial assets transferred by the Bank (securitization) </div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank transferred financial assets (loans) to trusts for the purpose of issuing and selling securities for which collection is guaranteed by the cash flow resulting from such assets or group of assets. Through this way the funds that were originally used by the Bank to finance the loans are obtained earlier. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of December&#160;31, 2023 and 2022, considering the latest available accounting information as of the date of issuance of these consolidated Financial Statements, the assets managed through Macro Fiducia SAU (subsidiary) of this type of trusts amounted to <ix:nonFraction name="bma:FinancialAssetsSecuritizedTransferred" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122098">2,636</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:FinancialAssetsSecuritizedTransferred" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122099">36,372</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. </div> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><ix:exclude>BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:7%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">45.3</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Trusts guaranteeing loans granted by the Bank </div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As it is common in the Argentine banking market, the Bank requires, in some cases, that the debtors present certain assets or entitlements to receive assets in a trust as a guarantee for the loans granted. This way, the risk of losses is minimized and access to the security is guaranteed in case of the debtor&#8217;s non-compliance. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Trusts usually act as conduits to collect cash from the debtor&#8217;s flow of operations and send such cash to the Bank for the payment of the debtor&#8217;s loans and thus ensure compliance with the obligations assumed by the trustor and guaranteed through the trust. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Additionally, other guarantee trusts manage specific assets, mainly real property. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Provided there is no non-compliance or delays by the debtor in the obligations assumed with the beneficiary, the trustee shall not execute the guarantee and all excess amounts as to the value of the obligations are reimbursed by the trustee to the debtor. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of December&#160;31, 2023 and 2022, considering the latest available accounting information as of the date of issuance of these consolidated Financial Statements, the assets managed by Banco Macro SA and Macro Fiducia SAU, amounted to <ix:nonFraction name="bma:FinancialAssetsManagedByBank" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122101">801,979</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:FinancialAssetsManagedByBank" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122102">8,474,233</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:7%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">45.4</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Trusts in which the Bank acts as Trustee (Management) </div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank, through its subsidiaries, performs management duties of the corpus assets directly according to the agreements, performing only trustee duties and has no other interests in the trust. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In no case shall the Trustee be liable with its own assets or for any obligation deriving from the performance as trustee. Such obligations do not imply any type of indebtedness or commitment for the trustee and they will be fulfilled only through trust assets. In addition, the trustee will not encumber the corpus assets or dispose of them beyond the limits established in the related trust agreements. The fees earned by the Bank from its role as trustee are calculated according to the terms and conditions of the agreements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Trusts usually manage funds derived from the activities performed by trustors, for the following main purposes: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Tax claims </div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The AFIP and tax authorities of the relevant jurisdictions have reviewed the tax returns filed by the Bank related to income tax, minimum presumed income tax and other taxes (mainly turnover tax). However, in March 2013, when BPI had already been merged with and into the Bank, the trial court resolved to amend the terms of the agreement and ordered the reimbursement of amounts of money to a larger number of clients as compared to the number arising from the terms approved by the court in due time. Such resolution was appealed by the Bank as BPI&#8217;s surviving company. The appeal was dismissed by the Court of Appeals, which abrogated both the trial court decision and the court-approved agreement, thus ordering the Bank to answer the complaint. This gave rise to the filing of an extraordinary appeal against such decision as well as the subsequent filing of a complaint for the extraordinary appeal denied. On May&#160;5, 2021, the Bank was notified of the dismissal of the complaint appeal, ordering the return of the main process to the CNACAF for continuing with the proceedings, who also submitted them to the trial court, which received them on 09/27/2021 and were requested as effectum vivendi in proceedings &#8220;Estado Nacional &#8211; Ministerio Producci&#243;n de la Naci&#243;n c/ Asociaci&#243;n de Defensa de los Consumidores y Usuarios de la R.A y otros s/Ordinario&#8221; (File No.&#160;6757/2013), in which the Bank is not a party, by the commercial court, clerk&#8217;s office No.&#160;11. <td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, CORPORATE GOVERNANCE TRANSPARENCY POLICY AND RISK MANAGEMENT </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As a financial institution, the activities of Banco Macro SA are governed by Financial Entities Law No.&#160;21526, as supplemented, and the regulations issued by the BCRA. Moreover, the Bank adheres to the good banking practices included in the Financial Entities Corporate Governance Guidelines, as supplemented of the BCRA. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank publicly trades its shares on the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange (BCBA, for its acronym in Spanish) and, thus, it is subject to the regulations issued by the CNV. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Through General Resolution No.&#160;797/19, the CNV established the minimum contents of the Corporate Governance Code, adding notions of good corporate governance to corporate management as guidelines or recommendations that seek to provide transparency thereto. The CNV annually requires the issuance of a report in which financial institutions have to explain how the recommendations are implemented or to explain the reasons why it decided not to adopt the good practices described in such resolution. The Bank annually publishes a document called Corporate Governance Explanatory Report together with the Annual Report to the Shareholders for the fiscal year, required by regulations, which is available on the Bank&#8217;s website and on that of such enforcement agency. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This regulation reinforces the notions contained in Capital Markets Law establishing principles such as &#8220;full disclosure&#8221;, &#8220;transparency&#8221;, &#8220;efficiency&#8221;, &#8220;public investor protection&#8221;, &#8220;equal footing between investors&#8221; and &#8220;protection of the stability of financial entities and financial intermediaries&#8221;. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On the other hand, as the Bank lists its shares on the NYSE, qualifying as a foreign private issuer, it is required to comply with certain corporate governance standards as established in section 303A of the NYSE&#8217;s Listed Company Manual, as amended. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The main guidelines under the BCRA standards contemplated in the revised text &#8220;Financial Entities Corporate Governance Guidelines&#8221;, as supplemented, are as follows. (The information included in this section may not be entirely applicable to Banco BMA SAU (formerly known as Banco Ita&#250; Argentina SA), BMA Asset Management SA (formerly known as Ita&#250; Asset Management SA) and BMA Valores SA (formerly known as Ita&#250; <td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Anticorruption policy </div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Pursuant to Law No.&#160;27401 (Law on Corporate Criminal Liability), the Board establishes that officers and employees of the Bank and its subsidiaries shall not offer to pay, pay or authorize the payment of money or anything of value to (public) officers to obtain or keep a business. It also extends these guidelines to the private sphere. These principles are contained in the Code of Ethics for directors and senior managers, and the Code of Conduct for all employees. Besides, the Bank has a Code of Conduct for suppliers. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The laws of other jurisdictions with similar prohibitions apply, especially the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), because Banco Macro SA is a foreign company that lists its shares in the NYSE and is subject to SEC control and oversight. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Group companies that wish to perform any transaction involving any public administration officer, public agency or public company, either Argentine or foreign, shall communicate this event in advance to the Board through the General Manager and inform, before the transaction is conducted, the agents or intermediaries that may be involved in the transaction. The Bank also has a manual with guidelines for interacting with public officers. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This communication duty is not mandatory for the transactions derived from agreements with provincial financial agents (except for the subscription of framework agreements), ordinary bank transactions (for example, payroll processing) and the transactions that do not pose any major risk due to the minimum amounts involved. </div><div style="margin-top: 0px; Such transactions are carried out under usual market conditions. See also Note 20. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Under current Argentine legislation, directors are required to perform their duties with the loyalty and diligence of a prudent businessman. Directors are jointly and severally liable to the Bank, the shareholders and third parties for a poor performance of duties and infringements to the law, bylaws and regulations, as the case may be, and are responsible for repairing the damages caused by fraud, abuse of authority or negligence. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The loyalty duties of a director are considered to include: (i)&#160;the ban from using corporate assets and the confidential information to which he/she may have access for personal purposes; (ii)&#160;the ban from taking advantage or, due to errors or omissions, allowing a third party to take advantage of the Bank&#8217;s business opportunities, (iii)&#160;the obligation of acting as director only for the purposes established in the law, the Bank&#8217;s bylaws or the intention of the shareholders or the Board of Directors; and (iv)&#160;the obligation of taking extreme care so that the acts conducted by the Board of Directors have no direct or indirect effects against the Bank&#8217;s interests. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A director should notify the Board of Directors and the Audit Committee about any conflict of interest such director may have in a transaction proposal and should refrain from voting on the matter. </div><div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

The Bank has appointed a Risk Manager who reports directly to the Board of Directors. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Its duties include ensuring that an independent risk management be established, establishing policies, procedures and measurement methodologies and report systems which allow the identification, measurement and monitoring of the risk under its charge and also the duties of each organizational level in the process. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The risk management process includes the establishment of the exposure limits for each risk by the Board of Directors, a follow-up on the exposure to each limit by the persons in charge, the preparation of regular reports for the Risk Management Committee, a follow-up on the alerts and the implementation of action plans regarding the alerts and the guidelines for developing stress tests. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The system supplements the policies and procedures specific to each risk (Financial, Credit, Operational, Counterparty Credit, Country Risk, Securitization, Reputational, Compliance, Strategic Risks, among others). </div><div style="margin-top: 0px; Credit Risk Management reports functionally to the General Manager. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Risk Management</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Risk Management area is in charge of the Financial Risk, Credit Risk and Operating and Technology Risk areas. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The main procedures carried out by the Risk Management Department are: </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:8%">&#160;</td>
