<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Stress tests </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:11%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The process of stress test includes documenting and formalizing the program as well as the persons in charge of carrying it out, the frequency of testing and the validation of the system. It also contemplates the Contingency Plan based on the test results. The Risk Management Committee leads and coordinates this application. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

The methods used to deal with subsidiaries are exactly the same. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:11%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The economic capital sufficiency evaluation process is an integral part of the corporate governance and risk management culture of the entities. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:11%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Quantified economic capital was implemented as a formal procedure, both currently and prospectively, and is a tool used in the day-to-day management of risks, in preparing the Business Plan and the Stress Tests. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:11%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The methods used to measure the economic capital of each risk were documented and approved by the Management, pursuant to the internal rules on Corporate Governance and Risk Management. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:11%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The results must serve to support decision-making, including strategic decisions adopted by the Board and the Senior Management. <td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">52.1</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Credit Risk</div> </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Credit risk is the risk that the Bank incurs a loss because its customers or counterparties fail to discharge their contractual obligations. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank manages and controls credit risk by setting limits on the amount of risk it is willing to accept and by establishing indicators for monitoring. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Board approves the credit and risk assessment policy to provide a framework to generate businesses to achieve a proper relationship between the risk assumed and profitability. The Bank has procedure manuals detailing the related guidelines, compliance with effective regulations and limits set. The goals are: </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Enhancing the quality of the risk assumed, with proper guarantees according to the term of the loan and the level of risk involved. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:15%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8226;</td>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Monitoring on an ongoing basis the loan portfolio and customer level of compliance. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Credit risk management involves the existence of a structure with the characteristics needed to attain the organizational goals during the stages of the credit cycle: admission, follow-up, monitoring and recovery. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The risk assessment process is differentiated based on whether customers belong to Corporate Banking or Retail Banking. </div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center"><ix:exclude>9<div style="display:inline;">7</div></ix:exclude></div></ix:continuation> </div> </div> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_32" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_33"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_33" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_34"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_34" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_35"><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div> </div> </div> <div> <div> <div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"> <div style="text-align:center"> <div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_35" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_36"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To assess Corporate Banking customers, the Bank has different methods involving different responsibility levels that become increasingly complex according to the size of the transactions in terms of assistance types and amounts, weighed by terms and hedges with guarantees. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For the authorization of assistance involving small amounts, self-liquidating collaterals or temporary assistance, the Bank grants special credit powers, on a personal basis, to higher-ranking officials based on their knowledge, experience and training. At any rate, the use of these powers is associated with the outcome of an objective assessment, avoiding any discretion in the credit approvals. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To grant predefined products and restricted amounts to the Small Companies and Agro segments, the Bank has standardized assessment systems that are used on a decentralized manner and include origination scoring and screening methods to admit and assign limits, based on the customers&#8217; economic, financial and equity information. There is also a centralized massive qualification periodic process that Credit Risk Management makes available to branches on a continuous basis. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">When transactions in amount the instances of authorization by delegated powers or through the decentralized risk analysis, ratings are approved in the Credit Committees. The powers vested on the different decision-making bodies are continuously reviewed to adjust them to the Bank&#8217;s volume of transactions and thus improve credit rating. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The risk analysis of assistance addressed in the Credit Committees is carried out at the Corporate Risk Management Department by specialized risk analysts that prepare separate risk reports per customer or group of companies, which are provided to Committee members to support the credit decisions made. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Risk reports include, at least, information regarding the use of loans and their source of repayment, the debtor&#8217;s historical and current behavior and the group of companies to which it belongs; the debtor&#8217;s repayment capacity based on cash flows; the guarantees that will cover the transactions, the ownership status, the enforcement possibilities and their sensibility to the changes in the economy; the market in which the debtor operates and the debtor&#8217;s position, and the debtor&#8217;s equity, economic and financial position and possibility of accessing loans. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Committees&#8217; resolutions include the terms and conditions applicable to the assistance in terms of the amount, currency, terms, guarantees and follow-up provisions, among others. The decisions are based on the debtor&#8217;s cash flows and payment capacity and only to a secondary extent on debtor&#8217;s equity and risk mitigating factors. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Credit risk assessment for Retail Banking customers, is governed by specific policies that consider customers&#8217; inclusion in one of the following segments: </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Open Market customers. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To speed up origination circuits, the Credit Risk Management has widened the use of scoring methods, which impose a minimum limit for the customer to be admitted for credit purposes, considering an acceptable delinquency level. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Consumer portfolio qualifications are available on a permanent basis to branches in the system called Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and to customers through digital channels, which allows operating within the limits and conditions approved by the Credit Risk Management on a centralized basis. This modality restricts the operating risks that are inherent to the assessment. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For new non-prequalified customers, the originator enters the requested transactions in the risk assessment system related to the customer segment, which approves or rejects the transaction; if approved, maximum assistance amounts by product are provided. Assessment systems are mainly based on an admission and certain maximum indebtedness rules and installment/income ratio. The assessment systems are based mainly on a qualification score and certain maximum indebtedness and installment/income relationship rules. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">There are specific rules regarding the debtor&#8217;s file integration to duly document the data entered into the assessment systems. Credit risk officers also define a credit power system based on the margins to be approved and, if applicable, the exceptions admitted. </div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; In addition, as part of the assessment process, the exception flow and the control of credit powers are also automated. These actions managed to reduce operating risks and allowed tracing transactions and their approval levels. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The Bank adopts processes to detect interrelated debtor groups with correlated risk (group of companies) and to group risk exposures with the same debtor or counterparty in different lines of credit. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Before the transactions are settled, a series of controls are implemented to reduce related credit and operating risks and classify transactions within the technical relationships regulatory framework. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The Bank implements a formal, robust and well-defined process to manage nonperforming loans. These procedures are differentiated based on the type of portfolio and delinquency status. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">To mitigate credit risk, guarantees are requested on agreed financing. A particular area of the Credit Risk Management Department manages all guarantees received by the Bank and assesses and updates regularly the appraisal value and effective term to monitor the quality of risk mitigators. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Credit risk allowances of the loan portfolio</div> </div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;text-indent: 0px;display:inline;">As from 2020, the Bank&#8217;s policy concerning credit risk allowances is based on the calculation of ECL based on analytical models (statistical models related to loan portfolio management) pursuant to IFRS 9. According to the guidelines in section 5.5. on Impairment (including the principles and methods to recognize ECL due to significant increases in credit risk and the subsequent impairment of financial assets for ECL), the Bank recognizes the impairment of its financial assets.</div></div></div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; <td style="background-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0);background-color:rgba(255, 255, 255, 0);">&#160;</td> </tr> </table> </ix:nonNumeric> <div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Credit Risk Management manages credit risk, which consists of identifying, assessing, following up, controlling and mitigating this risk across credit cycle stages. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Credit Risk Management Office designs and develops ECL models. It reports to the Credit Risk Management, which is also in charge of designing and calculating rating and scoring models to quantify credit risk and the measures to calculate PD, EAD and LGD, as well as other models to calculate the impact of the prospective view. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Administration and Credit Operation Management, through the Credit Review area, analyze the entire portfolio under individual assessment and classifies customers in different credit risk stages. Together with the Corporate Risk and Credit Recovery Management Departments (that contribute their view from a standpoint of risk assessment and recovery management), they calculate ECL for corporate customers in stage 2 and stage 3. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The definitions and assessment of ECL are regularly presented to the Risk Management Committee, which approves the model methodologies, adjustments and validation. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td>&#160;</td> </tr> </table> </ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric> <ix:continuation id="TextSelection_112972808" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112972808_1"><div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Exposure at default (EAD)</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The EAD represents the exposure of a financial instrument on the date of the analysis, i.e. the level to which the Bank is exposed to credit risk in the event of a potential default by the counterparty. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To calculate the EAD, segmentation is performed at product level, according to the following differentiation: </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:22%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Products with no exposure certainty: in the case of revolving products (credit cards and saving accounts) in stages 1 and 2, in order to calculate the EAD, it is necessary to estimate a credit conversion factor (CCF). For these transactions, the CCF represents the average percentage of exposure increase that may be observed in a contract from measurement to default. For these products, in stage 3, no additional increase is considered in the exposure. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Products with exposure certainty: in these types of products (generally amortizable loans), future exposure is known because the counterparty cannot increase its exposure beyond what was agreed upon in the contractual schedule. Therefore, the CCF does not apply to these products, and the EAD varies at each moment in time by reflecting the amortization of the loan balance due. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Loss given default (LGD)</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">LGD is the estimated loss in the case of default. It is based on the difference between all contractual cash flows and the cash flows expected by the lender (i.e., all cash shortfalls), considering the proceeds from the realization of collateral. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">It is the supplement to the unit of the recovery rate; that is, the proportion not collected by the Bank with respect to the EAD. Consequently, the amount at default is compared with the present value of the amounts recovered after the date of default. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">LGD varies based on the type of counterparty, aging, type of claim and the existence of guarantees securing credits. It is expressed as a percentage of the loss for EAD. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Just as the PDs, to assess the LGD, a distinction is made per customer in individual analyses and per product in the case of customers analyzed collectively. The Bank bases its estimates on the historical information observed regarding the recoveries obtained on customers or default transactions, discounted at the effective interest rate of such agreements and measured upon default. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Once the recovery rates are obtained, this behavior is projected through the triangle method to estimate the periods with less maturity. Finally, the weighted average of the loss for each portfolio is determined. </div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center"><ix:exclude>10<div style="display:inline;">2</div></ix:exclude></div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation> </div> </div> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112972808_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112972808_2"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_54" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_55"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Customers analyzed on an individual basis</div>: </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To make such an assessment, some objective data were defined to analyze whether there is a SICR and to determine whether it should be reclassified to stage 2 or to stage 3 when a default is produced or expected, or whether they should remain in stage 1. <td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Cash flows analysis shows that it is highly unlikely that the customer may meet all its obligations in the agreed-upon conditions. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Credit Administration and Transactions Department analyzes all the portfolio under this approach, with special emphasis on customers in stages 2 and 3 in the previous month and those showing objective data that could evidence the existence of a SICR. The study is supplemented with the macroeconomic context and other news in relation to the performance of customers. Its staging proposal is submitted to the consideration of Corporate Risk and Credit Recovery Management Departments, which incorporate their own vision of the customer or the activity sector. The final assessment of the stage assigned to each customer is approved by the Credit Risk Management and is used as an input to estimate the ECL of the customers analyzed on an individual basis. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">ECL calculation for customers included in an individual analysis</div>: </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Stage 1: the estimates of the customers classified in stage 1 arise from the parameters under expected credit loss models, whose characteristics are described in the previous sections on PD, EAD and LGD. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Stages 2 and 3: based on the evidence gathered upon the analysis, the Credit Risk Management &#8211;considering the level of progress of collection negotiations, as well as the evidence from a potential sale of collateral received or other credit improvements making up the contractual terms&#8211; prepares three potential recovery scenarios for each credit transaction of stage 2 and 3 customers, calculating the current value of expected flows for each scenario, which are weighted in view of their probability of occurrence. The expected loss of each transaction is the difference between the book payable of each transaction and the present weighted value of expected cash flows. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:13%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:7%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">52.1.2</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Prospective information used in ECL models</div> </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The calculation of ECL for risk impairment includes and is adjusted prospectively with respect to the portfolio behavior. To such end, the Bank examines the macroeconomics variables which have an impact on PD and LGD and designed 4 models which differ by customer type: Retail, Agro, Pymes and Commercial. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The main economic variables that impact on the expected losses used to calculate ECL for each economic scenario are changes in GDP, changes in interest rates, among others. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As established in IFRS 9, impact is calculated based on the different behavior scenarios of the variables; to such end, a 36-month estimate on the variables used for the models is requested from a well-known economic consulting firm. This estimate is prepared for three alternative macroeconomic scenarios, to which a likelihood of occurrence is assigned. </div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 20%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Finally, the Bank calculates ECL by applying the alternative scenarios on a weighted basis, which are updated at least on a quarterly basis in each calendar quarter. </div></div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The value of the macroeconomic variables used in calculating the forward-looking adjustment is restricted to econometric model calculations and the estimates of the independent consultant in relation to those variables. However, in line with the &#8220;Guidance on credit risk and accounting for expected credit losses&#8221; of the Basel Banking Supervision Committee, the Bank applies its own criterion based on experience in order to consider reasonable and sustainable prospective information in due manner (including macroeconomic factors) and, as applicable, to determine the proper level of value corrections. </div> <ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DisclosureOfKeyEconomicVariablesOrAssumptionExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_112968937" id="ixv-95909"> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:20%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The following table shows the estimated values for macroeconomic variables used in the models for each scenario (base case, alternative 1 and alternative 2), with the assigned probability of occurrence to each scenario: </div> </ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_112968937" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112968937_1"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_62" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_63"><ix:exclude> <div style="margin-top: 0px; <td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="text-align: left; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Overview of modified and forborne loans </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 20%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">From a risk management point of view, once an asset is forborne or modified, the Bank&#8217;s special department for distressed assets continues to monitor the exposure until it is completely and ultimately derecognized. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 20%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The amortized cost of loans modified during 2023 and the associated net modification amounted to <ix:nonFraction name="bma:AmortizedCostsOfFinancialAssetsModifiedDuringThePeriod" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122410">4,469,175</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:AmortizedCostsOfFinancialAssetsModifiedDuringThePeriod" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122411">558,063</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. The Bank does not consider loans using the mandatory extensions and payment facilities provide by BCRA as part of such modified loans. The amortized cost of loans modified during 2022 and the associated net modification amounted to <ix:nonFraction name="bma:NetModification" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122412">5,008,400</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:NetModification" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122413">1,343,724</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. </div></div></div> <div style="font-size: 12pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-size: 12pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div></div>

<td style="width: 7%; vertical-align: top;text-align:left;"><div style="display:inline;">52.1.4</div></td>
<td style="vertical-align: top;text-align:left;"> <div style="text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Additional Forward-looking allowances based on expert credit judgment</div> </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="clear:both;max-height:0pt;"></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 20%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Adjustment for uncertainty about conditions of accessing loans to MIPYMES and Federal Government Securities</div> </div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 20%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;text-indent: 0px;display:inline;">As of December&#160;31, 2022, the Bank decided to record an additional allowance for </div></div><ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:AdditionalAllowanceRecognisedInProfitOrLossAllowanceAccountForCreditLossesOfFinancialAssets" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022_CurrentScenarioFromNegativeRealInterestRatesMemberBMAEventAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122414">5,720,558</ix:nonFraction><div style="font-size: 10pt;display:inline;"> </div><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">based on the estimation of the impact that a change in the current scenario from negative real interest rates, in an accelerating inflationary context, would have on the ECL of the Mipymes portfolio, and as a consequence of the Bank&#8217;s Management assessment of the macroeconomic environment of Argentina, including the actions performed by the Federal Government to manage its debt instruments and certain uncertainty mainly related to the Bank&#8217;s long-term holdings of Federal Government instruments. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 20%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Adjustment for expectations of increased risk due to the change in economic policy</div> </div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 20%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">At the date of these consolidated Financial Statements, Management considered that there is uncertainty about the impacts that could arise from the change in the economic policy, the implementation of a macroeconomic imbalances adjustment program and an inflation stabilization plan. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 20%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">In particular, the temporary negative impact on the quality of the consumer credit portfolio, on the behavior of Mipymes and on the expected recovery of companies with credit-impaired, was analyzed. This impact would come from relative price adjustments, the elimination of subsidies on public services, and/or the presence of positive real interest rates, among other measures, until the stability of certain macroeconomic variables and a recovery of activity levels is achieved. </div></div></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 20%;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;text-indent: 0px;display:inline;">As abovementioned, the Bank decided to record an additional allowance for </div></div><ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:AdditionalAllowanceRecognisedInProfitOrLossAllowanceAccountForCreditLossesOfFinancialAssets" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022_NegativeImpactOnTheQualityOfConsumerCreditPortfolioAndTheBehaviousOfMipymesMemberBMAEventAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122415">10,978,134</ix:nonFraction><div style="font-size: 10pt;display:inline;">.</div></div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<td>&#160;</td></tr></table></ix:continuation> <div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Credit Risk </div></div><div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Different methodologies are used to calculate economic capital for Credit Risk (regulatory), depending on the size of the credit exposure. </div></div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In those exposures considered significant, the economic capital is calculated through a Montecarlo Simulation Process and allocated using the Covariance Methodology. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Montecarlo Simulation Process consists in generation of different losses scenarios. Each scenario represents a possible value of loss distribution. Calculating the difference between <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ExpectedCreditLossRate" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122727">99</ix:nonFraction>% percentile &#8211;unexpected loss&#8211; and the average value &#8211;expected loss&#8211; of such distribution, the economic capital is obtained. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For each scenario, the following parameters -exogenous to the simulation model- are taken as given: parameters of probability of default (&#8220;probability of default&#8221; or PD), loss given default (&#8220;loss given default&#8221; or LGD) and exposure values (&#8220;exposure at default&#8221; or EAD). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Additionally, a factor is incorporated &#8211;amplification or contraction of the debtor&#8217;s individual PD&#8211; that reflects the volatility of defaults by clients in a certain sector of activity (combination of economic activity and/or geographical area where activity is carried out) and the correlation between defaults of clients from different sectors of activity. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The advantage of this methodology is that it incorporates the effect of the concentration of exposures at the debtor level and at the portfolio level. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In those exposures considered not significant, the economic capital requirement is obtained using the Vasicek Model, as present in the final Basel II (2004)&#160;document. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the case of significant wholesale exposures, the Economic Capital by credit risk of each exposure can be decomposed into three risk factors inherent to each exposure: </div><div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:14%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Economic Capital by individual concentration risk: refers to the exacerbation in the magnitude of economic capital derived from the existence of concentration in terms of exposure to a particular client. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:14%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Economic Capital by risk of sectoral concentration: represents the exacerbation in the magnitude of economic capital generated from the existence of concentration of exposures in the same sector of economic activity. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:14%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8226;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Economic Capital by systemic risk: fraction of capital that would be obtained if the portfolio is diversified both at the sectoral and individual level. It represents non-diversifiable risk. </div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Economic Capital by individual concentration risk is defined as the quotient between the variance of the client&#8217;s simulated loss and the variance of the total simulated loss. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Economic Capital by sector concentration risk represents the exacerbation in the magnitude of the covariance between the loss of a certain client and the loss of the portfolio due to not having a diversified portfolio and is expressed as a proportion with respect to the variance of the total loss. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Finally, the Economic Capital by systemic risk is calculated as the remaining capital once the individual concentration risk and sector risk components have been subtracted. </div><div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center"><ix:exclude>10<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">8</div></ix:exclude></div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_80" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_81"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_81" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_82"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_82" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_83"><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_83" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_84"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><ix:exclude>BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Additionally, a concentration surcharge is considered for non-significant retail and wholesale positions that is supported by Vasicek&#8217;s formulations. The individual concentration surcharge is calculated as an additional amount on the capital requirements of the aforementioned positions using a coefficient &#945; that, depending on the Herfindahl index (HHI) of the same portfolio and the probability of default (PD) of the accredited entities that form it, takes a certain value. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Counterparty Risk </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">To calculate the Economic Capital by Counterparty Credit Risk, a simulation model is applied, which reflects the impact of the interdependence between counterparties with similar characteristics. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For this risk, it is necessary to define the EAD of each type of operation. This parameter is necessary for the calculation of the Capital to be allocated. Once the EADs associated with the operations that generate Counterparty Risk are obtained, these values are added at the client level and added to the EADs at the client level generated by traditional credit operations. This vector of EADs at the client level is what is considered for the calculation of Economic Capital by Credit Risk. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 13%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Securitization Risk </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The debt securities represent collection rights on the assets of the trust, under the conditions established in the prospectus and/or constitutive contract. There may be different types of debt securities with different collection preferences and conditions. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">A debt security generates exposure to Credit Risk and exposure to Interest Rate Risk, in the same way as a traditional credit operation does. The calculation and allocation methodologies of Economic Capital for this type of operations, it consists of including operations within the portfolios for which Economic Capital by Credit Risk and Interest Rate Risk are calculated and allocating a portion of the capital calculated based on the incidence of the potential losses that such operations could generate in the total losses of the portfolio. </div><div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:7%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">52.2</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Liquidity Risk</div> </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The liquidity risk is defined as the possibility that the Bank may not be able to comply with expected and unexpected current and future cash flows effectively, as well as guarantees, without affecting daily transactions or its financial position. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, the market liquidity risk refers to the risk that the Bank may not be able to clear or delete a position at market price: </div><div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:7%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">52.3</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Market Risk</div> </div></div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Market risk is defined as the possibility of suffering losses in positions on and off the Bank&#8217;s balance sheet as a result of the adverse fluctuations in the market prices of different assets. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Market risks arise from interest rate, currency and price positions, all of which are exposed to general and specific market changes and changes in the price volatility such as interest rates, credit margins, foreign currency exchange rates and prices of shares and securities, among others. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank determines the market risk exposure arising from the fluctuation in the value of portfolios of investments for trading, which result from changes in market prices, the Bank&#8217;s net positions in foreign currency, and government and private securities with normal quoted prices. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">These risks arise from the size of the Bank&#8217;s net positions and/or the volatility of the risk factors involved in each financial instrument. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank features Market Risk Management Policies in which the Bank establishes the proceedings to monitor and control risks derived from the variations in the quotes of financial instruments in order to optimize the risk-return ratio, making use of the appropriate structure of limits, models and management tools. In addition, the Bank features proper tools and proceedings allowing the Risk Management Committee and the Assets and Liabilities Committee to measure and administer this risk. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Risks to which those investment portfolios are exposed are monitored through Montecarlo simulation techniques of &#8220;Value at Risk&#8221; (VaR). The Bank applies the VaR methodology to calculate the market risk of the main positions adopted and the expected maximum loss based on a series of assumptions for a variety of changes in market conditions. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In order to carry out the abovementioned simulation, the Bank needs to have the Price historical series of those instruments that compose the portfolio. </div> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center"><ix:exclude>11<div style="display:inline;">2</div></ix:exclude></div></ix:continuation> </div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_95" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_96"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_96" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_97"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_97" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_98"><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_98" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_99"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: center;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><ix:exclude>BANCO MACRO SA AND ITS SUBSIDIARIES</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Prices are corrected by purging the effects of coupon payments and dividend payments, in the case of shares, in order to avoid affecting returns. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The method consists in creating return or price scenarios concerning an asset through the generation of random numbers. This is based on the selection of a stochastic model describing the performance of prices for each asset with the resulting specification of certain parameters required for calculation purposes. The model used is the geometric Brownian motion. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Once all &#8220;n&#8221; potential scenarios are obtained for valued positions, the P&amp;L vector must be calculated as the difference between the estimated value of the future portfolio and its value upon calculation. Then profit and loss will be placed in order to obtain the value at risk according to the <ix:nonFraction name="bma:PercentageOfConfidenceLevel" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122927">99</ix:nonFraction>% percentage applied. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Finally, the Economic Capital by market risk is obtained as the difference between the current value of the portfolio and the critical value previously obtained. </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:7%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">52.4</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Interest Rate Risk</div> </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The interest rate risk is defined as the possibility that changes occur in the Bank&#8217;s financial condition as a result of adverse interest rate fluctuations with a negative impact on the Shareholders&#8217; equity and profit or loss. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Within the framework of the interest rate risk management the Bank features a series of policies, procedures and internal controls included in the Structural Risk Management. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Bank monitors the net present value of its assets, liabilities and off balance sheet items, upon certain disturbance scenarios and interest rate stress through Montecarlo simulation techniques. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For this purpose, the maximum potential loss is determined considering a temporal line of three months and <ix:nonFraction name="bma:PercentageOfConfidenceLevel" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122928">99</ix:nonFraction>% confidence level interval. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Equity Value Model (EVM) is determined as the net sum of cash flows (interest and principal losses) that the Bank can generate, discounted at market interest rate curve. If the market interest rate curve used for the discount is affected, the effect of such variation impacts directly on the value of the Bank. Generally speaking, reports related to EVM seek to analyze the Bank&#8217;s long-term solvency. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">It is noteworthy that the use of that approach does not avoid losses beyond those limits in the event of the most significant market changes. </div><ix:nonNumeric name="bma:DisclosureOfBanksVarByTypeOfRiskExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-102675"> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">As of December&#160;31, 2023 and 2022, the Bank&#8217;s economic capital by type of risk is as follows: </div> <div style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:6%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">52.6</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Operational Risk</div> </div></div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Operational risk is defined as the risk of loss arising from the inadequacy or failure of internal processes, human errors and/or internal system failures, or those originated by external events. This definition includes the Legal Risk but excludes the Strategic Risk and Reputational Risk. </div> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center"><ix:exclude>11<div style="display:inline;">3</div></ix:exclude></div></ix:continuation> </div></div> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_99" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_100"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_100" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_101"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_101" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_102"><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div> <div> <div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"> <div style="text-align:center"> <div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_102" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_103"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Within such framework, the legal risk (which may occur from within the Bank or externally) comprises, among other aspects, the exposure to penalties, sanctions or other economic consequences or results for failure to comply with any rule or regulation or contractual obligation. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">On the other hand, the Bank implemented an operational risk management system that meets the guidelines and provisions established by the BCRA in its Communiqu&#233; &#8220;A&#8221; 5398, as amended, and under Communiqu&#233; &#8220;A&#8221; 5272 the BCRA provided for a minimum capital requirement under this description, effective as of February&#160;1, 2012. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The operating risk management system is formed by: </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

With such reports the Risk Management Department communicates the results of the follow-up of the management of the main risks to which the Bank is exposed. Each report contains information on risk measurement, evolution, trends, principal exposures, control of main limits and the capital level required for each type of risk. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:24%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">At the meeting of the Risk Management Committee, the Comprehensive Risk Management Department shall submit for consideration the results of the performance of such department and the reports issued during the period under analysis. The resolutions adopted by the Committee shall be recorded in Minutes to be considered by the Board of Directors, who shall subsequently approve, in this manner, the performance and risk level of the analyzed period. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Entity has a methodology for Economic Capital calculation for operational risk. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Economic Capital for operational risk will arise from a simulation engine, which will produce a distribution of total losses for operational risk. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In this manner, the Economic Capital can be arrived at, which is calculated from the resulting difference between the Maximum Loss (associated with a <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ExpectedCreditLossRate" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122936">99.9</ix:nonFraction>% confidence level) and the Expected Loss of said distribution. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Taking into account that the Holding Period is the time it takes to change the risk profile of the portfolio, in the case of Operational Risk this concept is very variable, since it depends on each risk (for example, it does not take the same in taking out insurance than in improving processes to avoid fraud by third parties with retirees). In this sense, one year will be taken as the evaluation period, respecting normal market practice. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Furthermore, this methodology contemplates the allocation of economic capital to different risks, considering the concentration effect of processes in one or more suppliers. </div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center"><ix:exclude>11<div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">4</div></ix:exclude></div></ix:continuation> </div> </div> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_103" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_112971621_104"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; <td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; text-align: left; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">CHANGES IN THE ARGENTINE MACROECONOMIC ENVIRONMENT AND FINANCIAL AND CAPITAL MARKETS </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In the last years, the Argentine financial market has observed a prolonged period of volatility in the market <div style="text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">prices</div> of public and private financial instruments, including a high level of country risk, an increase in the official exchange rate between the Argentine peso and the US dollar, an increase in interest rates and a significant acceleration of the inflation rate (see Note 3. section &#8220;unit of measurement&#8221;). </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Particularly, related to the price of the US dollar, since the end of 2019 the gap between the official price of the US dollar -used mainly for foreign trade- and alternative market values began to widen significantly, having reached maximum peaks close to <ix:nonFraction name="bma:PercentageOfIncreaseDecreaseInForeignCurrency" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122938">200</ix:nonFraction>%. As of the date of issuance of these Financial Statements, the aforementioned gap amounts to approximately <ix:nonFraction name="bma:ActualGapBetweenDollarUsedForForeignTradeAndAlternativeMarketValues" contextRef="P12_31_2019To12_31_2019" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122939">18</ix:nonFraction>%. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Regarding the administration of the national public debt, a restructuring process has been observed, including various voluntary exchanges and agreements reached regarding debts with the Paris Club and the International Monetary Fund. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In this context, on December&#160;10, 2023, the new authorities of the Argentine national government took office and issued a series of emergency measures. Among the main objectives, among other relevant issues, is a regulatory flexibility in economic matters, reduction of the fiscal deficit mainly through a reduction in spending, including reduction of different types of subsidies. Likewise, there was a devaluation of the Argentine peso close to <ix:nonFraction name="bma:DevaluationOfTheCurrencyWithRespectToUsDollarPercentage" contextRef="P12_10_2023To12_10_2023_ARSsrtCurrencyAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122940">55</ix:nonFraction>% against to the US dollar<div style="text-indent: 0px; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#160;(going the price of the US dollar from Ps. <ix:nonFraction name="bma:DevaluationOfArgentinePesoWithRespectToUsDollar" contextRef="P12_13_2023To12_13_2023_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="2" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122941">366.50</ix:nonFraction> to Ps. <ix:nonFraction name="bma:DevaluationOfArgentinePesoWithRespectToUsDollar" contextRef="P12_13_2023To12_13_2023_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="2" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122942">799.95</ix:nonFraction> on December 13, 2023),</div> which has generated an acceleration of the inflation rate, with interannual inflation measured from the national CPI published by INDEC being <ix:nonFraction name="bma:AccelarationOfInterannualInflationRatePercentage" contextRef="P12_31_2023To12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-122943">288</ix:nonFraction>% at the date of issue of these consolidated Financial Statements. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The comprehensive program pursued by the new national government includes reforms in the economy, justice, foreign relations, infrastructure and others. On December&#160;20, 2023, through Decree of Necessity and Urgency No.&#160;70/2023, a significant number of reforms were established, regarding which different actors presented various protections or unconstitutionality requests to Justice to stop their application. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:7%; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">In addition, the local and international macroeconomic context generates certain degree of uncertainty regarding its future progress, considering the level of the global economic recovery. </div> <ix:exclude> <div style="margin-top: 0px;
